Matrix of Coefficients in a Linear Model

Source: R/Kmatrix.R
Kmatrix.Rd

This function obtains a matrix of coefficients (the linear functions \(K\) such that the predicted means are \(K\hat\beta\)) for models such as aov, lm, glm, gls, lme, lmer, glmer, glmmTMB, gam (package mgcv) and semireg.

The predicted means are built on a reference grid: every combination of the factor levels in the model, with covariates fixed at their means (or other chosen values). Each row of K is the equally weighted average of the grid rows for one level combination of modelterm. The design matrix of the grid is evaluated with the model's own stored basis information, so covariates may enter the model through transformations such as poly(x, 2), ns(x, 3), bs(x), log(x), scale(x) or I(x^2), only through interactions (e.g. A:x without x, or x:z), or through smooth terms (s(x), te(x, z), s(x, by = A)) of a gam.

Usage

Kmatrix(model, modelterm, covariate=NULL, covariateV=NULL, data=NULL, prtnum=FALSE,
        cov_reduce=mean, exclude=NULL,
        weights=c("equal", "proportional", "outer", "cells", "flat"))

Arguments

model

Model object returned by aov, lm, glm, gls, lme, lmer, glmer, glmmTMB, gam/bam (package mgcv; for gamm use its $gam component) or semireg.

modelterm

Name (in "quotes") for indicating which model term's predicted mean to be calculated. The modelterm must be given exactly as it appears in the printed model, e.g. "A" or "A:B". A factor created in the model formula, e.g. factor(dose), can be given either as "factor(dose)" or as "dose".

covariate

A numerical vector to specify values of covariates for calculating predicted means, default values are the means of the associated covariates. It also can be the name of one or more covariates in the model, in which case predictions are made over a range of values of those covariates (see covariateV). For a semireg model this may also be a covariate that only appears in the smooth terms.

covariateV

Values for the covariate(s) named in covariate. For one covariate, a numeric vector. For several covariates, either a list of numeric vectors (all combinations are used) or a matrix with one named column per covariate, where each row is one prediction point (e.g. a set of locations for a two-dimensional smooth). When covariateV is NULL, 50 (one covariate) or 30 (several covariates) equally spaced values over the observed range are used.

data

In some cases, you need to provide the data set used in model fitting, for example when the data used to fit the model can no longer be found. Usually the data are recovered from the model.

prtnum

An option for printing covariate info on the screen or not. The default is FALSE.

cov_reduce

How covariates that are not varied are handled. A function returning a single value, applied to each covariate (the default mean; median is another choice), or the string "average", which averages the predictions over the observed values of those covariates instead of fixing them at one value. With "average", nonlinear terms such as poly(x, 2) or s(x) are averaged over the data, which for a gam gives predicted means adjusted for (rather than evaluated at the centre of) a spatial or temporal trend.

exclude

For gam models only: labels of smooth terms to leave out of the predictions (their columns of K are set to zero), e.g. "s(Block)". The default NULL excludes random-effect smooths (bs = "re" and bs = "fs"), so the predicted means are population-level means, as for lmer. Use exclude = character(0) to keep all smooth terms.

weights

How the cells of the factors that are not in modelterm are weighted when averaging over them: "equal" (the default; equal weights), "proportional" (weights proportional to the frequencies of those cells in the data, the same for every mean, as SAS LSMEANS / OM), "outer" (products of each factor's own frequencies), "cells" (each mean weights the cells by their own frequencies) or "flat" (equal weights over the non-empty cells). The definitions are those of emmeans.

Value

K

Coefficients matrix. It has an attribute "estimable", a logical vector with one value per row that is FALSE for rows that are not estimable functions of the model parameters (e.g. means for a missing cell in a rank-deficient model).

fctnames

A model frame contains factor(s) info in the model.

response

The name of response variable in the model.

preddf

The data of the predictor variables used in model fitting.

refgrid

The reference grid used to build K: a list with the grid data (grid), the sparse weight matrix W that averages grid rows into rows of K, and the rows of fctnames (target), and basis, the function that gives the model's basis for grid rows. Any other basis evaluated on grid, e.g. the smooth terms of a semireg model, can be averaged in the same way as W %*% basis.

References

Welham, S., Cullis, B., Gogel, B., Gilmour, A., & Thompson, R. (2004), Prediction in linear mixed models, Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics, 46(3), 325-347.

Author

This function heavily depends on the codes from package "lsmeans".

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  data(Oats, package="nlme")
# fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety+(1|Block/Variety), data=Oats)
  fm <- lme(yield ~ nitro*Variety, random=~1|Block/Variety, data=Oats)
  Kmatrix(fm, "Variety", prtnum=TRUE)$K
#> 
#>  The predicted means are estimated at 
#> nitro 
#>   0.3 
#>             (Intercept) nitro VarietyMarvellous VarietyVictory
#> Golden Rain           1   0.3                 0              0
#> Marvellous            1   0.3                 1              0
#> Victory               1   0.3                 0              1
#>             nitro:VarietyMarvellous nitro:VarietyVictory
#> Golden Rain                     0.0                  0.0
#> Marvellous                      0.3                  0.0
#> Victory                         0.0                  0.3
#> attr(,"estimable")
#> Golden Rain  Marvellous     Victory 
#>        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE 
  Kmatrix(fm, "Variety", 0.5, prtnum=TRUE)$K
#> 
#>  The predicted means are estimated at 
#> nitro 
#>   0.5 
#>             (Intercept) nitro VarietyMarvellous VarietyVictory

#> Marvellous                      0.5                  0.0
#> Victory                         0.0                  0.5
#> attr(,"estimable")

#> Victory:0.2                         0.0                  0.2
#> Victory:0.3                         0.0                  0.3
#> Victory:0.4                         0.0                  0.4
#> Victory:0.5                         0.0                  0.5
#> Victory:0.6                         0.0                  0.6
#> attr(,"estimable")

#>            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE 
#> Golden Rain:0.5 Golden Rain:0.6    Marvellous:0  Marvellous:0.1  Marvellous:0.2 
#>            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE 
#>  Marvellous:0.3  Marvellous:0.4  Marvellous:0.5  Marvellous:0.6       Victory:0

#>            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE 
#>     Victory:0.6 
#>            TRUE 

  # Covariates entering through transformations or only through interactions
  fm2 <- lm(yield ~ Block + Variety + poly(nitro, 2), data=Oats)
  Kmatrix(fm2, "Variety")$K
#>             (Intercept)       Block.L       Block.Q       Block.C       Block^4
#> Golden Rain           1 -6.938894e-17 -2.775558e-17 -6.938894e-18 -2.081668e-17
#> Marvellous            1 -6.938894e-17 -2.775558e-17 -6.938894e-18 -2.081668e-17
#> Victory               1 -6.938894e-17 -2.775558e-17 -6.938894e-18 -2.081668e-17
#>                   Block^5 VarietyMarvellous VarietyVictory poly(nitro, 2)1
#> Golden Rain -1.387779e-17                 0              0               0
#> Marvellous  -1.387779e-17                 1              0               0
#> Victory     -1.387779e-17                 0              1               0
#>             poly(nitro, 2)2
#> Golden Rain      -0.1473139
#> Marvellous       -0.1473139
#> Victory          -0.1473139
#> attr(,"estimable")
#> Golden Rain  Marvellous     Victory 
#>        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE 
  fm3 <- lm(yield ~ Variety + Variety:nitro, data=Oats)
  Kmatrix(fm3, "Variety", "nitro", covariateV=c(0, 0.3, 0.6))$K
#>                 (Intercept) VarietyMarvellous VarietyVictory
#> Golden Rain:0             1                 0              0
#> Golden Rain:0.3           1                 0              0
#> Golden Rain:0.6           1                 0              0
#> Marvellous:0              1                 1              0
#> Marvellous:0.3            1                 1              0
#> Marvellous:0.6            1                 1              0

#> Victory:0.6               1                 0              1

#> Golden Rain:0.3                      0.3                     0.0
#> Golden Rain:0.6                      0.6                     0.0
#> Marvellous:0                         0.0                     0.0
#> Marvellous:0.3                       0.0                     0.3
#> Marvellous:0.6                       0.0                     0.6
#> Victory:0                            0.0                     0.0
#> Victory:0.3                          0.0                     0.0
#> Victory:0.6                          0.0                     0.0
#>                 VarietyVictory:nitro

#> Golden Rain:0.3                  0.0
#> Golden Rain:0.6                  0.0
#> Marvellous:0                     0.0

#> Marvellous:0.6                   0.0

#> Victory:0.6                      0.6
#> attr(,"estimable")

#>            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE 
#>  Marvellous:0.6       Victory:0     Victory:0.3     Victory:0.6 
#>            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE 

  # A smooth term in an mgcv model, averaged over the observed nitro values
  if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE)) {
    fm4 <- mgcv::gam(yield ~ Variety + s(nitro, k = 4) + s(Block, bs = "re"), data = Oats)
    Kmatrix(fm4, "Variety", cov_reduce = "average")$K
  }
